title: Choose Film Diagram Studio's visual world
question: Select the operating language that should guide the full interface redesign.

options.label: The Production Binder
options.lineage: annotated camera-department binders and call-sheet inserts
options.thesis: A working production document—fast to mark up, impossible to mistake for a generic design tool.
options.viewport: A clear command rail, a generous drafting stage, and a compact inspector read like one disciplined field document.
options.risk: Can feel overly editorial if live controls are not visibly immediate.

raised.raise: Use its uncompromising information density for compact metadata and time-critical controls.
Make transform, aim, and cone relationships visibly legible as a connected system.

options.label: The Lighting Plot
options.lineage: professional gaffer plots and architectural drafting sheets
options.thesis: Every control earns its place on a precision plot, with the camera and light geometry as the hero.
options.viewport: A near-black stage surrounds a pale plan sheet, with tools indexed like disciplined technical instruments.
options.risk: Familiar to the category; it needs strong editing to feel owned rather than expected.

options.label: The Tension Rig
options.lineage: kinetic tensegrity sculpture and engineering force diagrams
options.thesis: A spatial control surface where aim, scale, and light cones read as linked forces.
options.viewport: An instrument-like stage makes every selected fixture feel connected to its diagrammed output.
options.case: Strongly supports on-set adjustment, but loses some document-level familiarity for planning and teaching.
options.risk: Could turn a practical tool into an abstract technical object.

options.label: Signal Index
options.lineage: data-sublime barcode fields and monochrome signal displays
options.case: It is fast and exact but lacks filmmaking warmth and easy general-audience entry.
options.risk: Would make the spatial planning work feel emotionally remote.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished dark technical editor with familiar sidebars and blue accents.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional professional diagramming workspace, executed at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Easy to use, but visually interchangeable with adjacent production tools.
